name: Anurag Dikshit
current_role: Philanthropist; founder and trustee of the Kusuma Trust (UK and Gibraltar)
profile: IIT Delhi computer-science graduate who co-founded PartyPoker.com in 1997 and wrote the betting software behind PartyGaming, which listed in London in 2005. He sold his remaining stake by January 2010 and has since focused on the Kusuma Trust, which funds education and children's organisations, mainly in India and Gibraltar.
interesting_fact: The Telegraph reported that in 2010 he and the Sainsbury family were Britain's biggest donors, each giving over GBP 100 million that year; by 2014 about GBP 172.4m had gone to the Kusuma Trust.
deep_cut_fact: Before PartyPoker he worked in the US as a systems analyst at CMC and as a consultant for WebSci and AT&T; he and his wife also set up the Kusuma Gallery at the V&A's Photography Centre. He grew up and went to school (De Nobili School) in Dhanbad.
notes: Low public profile; best route is via Kusuma Trust. Note 2008 US guilty plea (online gambling) and $300m forfeiture - avoid in outreach. Trust does not accept unsolicited funding applications.

name: Hu Zhirong
current_role: Chairman, controlling shareholder and legal representative of Warom Technology (华荣科技, SSE: 603855); chairman of Warom Group
profile: Born 1962, Hu Zhirong controls Warom Technology, a Shanghai-based maker of explosion-proof electrical equipment that also has professional-lighting and new-energy businesses. The group traces its origins to 1987, and the listed company went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in May 2017. Hu holds about 34% of the shares.
interesting_fact: Warom is led by its explosion-proof equipment business, which is used in hazardous oil, gas, chemical and mining settings, and it now also does professional lighting and new energy.
deep_cut_fact: Besides Warom, Hu is listed as executive director of Shanghai Zunrong Yacht Club (上海尊荣游艇俱乐部) and vice-chairman of Fuji Elevator (Sichuan), according to Warom's 2025 annual report.
notes: Low media profile. Best route is the board secretary's office (Song Zongbin, hrzhd@warom.com). Relevant to the energy theme (explosion-proof gear for oil and gas, plus new energy).

name: Xia Chaojia
current_role: Chairman of Hejia Group (禾嘉集团) per an older profile; current status not verified
profile: Sichuan (Chengdu) industrialist who took over a small, run-down neighbourhood factory in 1979 and built it into Hejia Group, which had more than 20 subsidiaries. Its controlled company, Hejia Co. (禾嘉股份), listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 1997. He appeared on Forbes' China mainland rich list for three years in a row.
interesting_fact: In 1998 the group acquired all of Sichuan Feiqiu Group, a large state-owned enterprise nicknamed 'Asia's king of balls' for its football manufacturing.
deep_cut_fact: He started in 1979 by taking over the street factory with 6,000 yuan of borrowed money.
notes: Only found an old profile (qianzhan.com); could not verify his current role or whether he is alive. Hejia Co. was later renamed/restructured, so check current filings.

name: Xue Junteng
current_role: Shareholder of Luolai Lifestyle Technology (罗莱生活, SZSE: 002293); held 7.79% after a March 2019 share sale
profile: Xue Junteng is a major individual shareholder of Luolai Lifestyle, China's large home-textile (bedding) maker, which is controlled by chairman Xue Weicheng. In March 2019 he agreed to sell 25.44 million shares (3.37%) to CA Fabric Investments and kept 58.78 million shares (7.79%). His exact family relationship to the Xue founders was not confirmed in the sources read.
interesting_fact: His 2019 stake sale went to CA Fabric Investments, bringing in an outside strategic investor at Luolai.
notes: No biography found. Listed with Xue Weibin as wealth-sharer, but no source found linking the two. Appears to be a passive shareholder, not an executive. Route via Luolai's IR office if needed.

name: Gong Mingjie
current_role: Chairman and legal representative of Longda Foodstuff Group (龙大食品集团), Laiyang, Shandong (as of 2020 filing)
profile: Gong Mingjie chairs Longda Foodstuff Group, the Laiyang, Shandong food-processing group that was the controlling shareholder of the listed meat company Longda Meat (later Longda Meishi, SZSE: 002726). As of 2020 he and Gong Xuebin together held 64.17% of the group. The group sold blocks of its stake in the listed company in 2019-2020.
interesting_fact: Longda Group is based in Longwangzhuang subdistrict of Laiyang, a Shandong city known for food processing.
notes: The 2020 filing lists Longda Group's phone, but no email/site was found. The listed company is now 'ST Longda' (2026). His current role was not verified after 2020.

name: Cheng Zhongfa
current_role: Chairman (per 2024 interview) and controlling shareholder of Shandong Taihe Technologies (泰和科技, SZSE: 300801), Zaozhuang
profile: Cheng Zhongfa (also written 程终发) controls Shandong Taihe Technologies, a Zaozhuang-based maker of water-treatment chemicals, including scale and corrosion inhibitors, biocides and electronic-grade chemicals. The company was founded about 20 years ago and says it aims to become a global leader in fine chemicals; about 60% of its water-treatment chemical sales are exports.
interesting_fact: Taihe has more than 500,000 tonnes a year of water-treatment chemical capacity and has been named a national manufacturing 'single champion'.
deep_cut_fact: Taihe's subsidiary Qingli New Materials (氢力新材料) captures by-product hydrogen from its caustic-soda process and uses it for power and heat. The company is also investing 410m yuan in new-energy battery materials (LiFSI, FEC).
notes: Hurun spells the name 程钟发; filings use 程终发. Relevant to the energy theme (hydrogen by-product, battery electrolyte materials). The 2025 H1 report names Yao Ya as company head, so his exact current title should be checked.

name: Shen Dongjun
current_role: Former chairman of Leysen Jewellery / TESIRO (莱绅通灵, SSE: 603900); stepped down as chairman in January 2022 but stayed on as a director at that time
profile: Shen Dongjun built TESIRO (通灵珠宝) from a Nanjing jeweller into a national diamond brand. In 2002 he partnered with Belgian firm EDT on a patented cut with 87-89 facets, and he became known on TV as 'the diamond king'. After a control contest he resigned as chairman in January 2022 and was replaced by Ma Jun.
interesting_fact: In July 2015 the Belgian royal house made him an Officer of the Order of Leopold, which was described as the first award at that grade to a Chinese businessman.
deep_cut_fact: TESIRO partnered with the Berlin International Film Festival from 2009, became a main partner in 2014, and launched a red-carpet collection in 2010. Shen also co-produced and made a cameo in the TV drama sequel to 'Diamond Lover' (克拉恋人).
notes: Avoid the 2021-22 control dispute. After stepping down he said he was enjoying the free time. No personal contact found; his current activities after 2022 are not verified.

name: V K Mathews
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, IBS Software / The IBS Group; owner and chairman of Calicut FC
profile: Valayil Korath Mathews is a Kerala-born aeronautical engineer (IIT Kanpur) who worked at Air India and then as a general manager at Emirates (1983-1997). He founded IBS Software in 1997, and it grew into a SaaS provider for airline operations, loyalty, cargo, hospitality and cruise. Blackstone is a backer of IBS, and Mathews remains executive chairman.
interesting_fact: In 2024 he launched Calicut FC, which won the inaugural Super League Kerala title, beating Forca Kochi 2-1 in the final. The club has said it aims to reach the I-League and ISL.
deep_cut_fact: In 1980 he taught computer science at the Military College for the Indian Army, then joined Air India as a systems analyst (1981-83), before 14 years at Emirates. He grew up in the village of Kizhakkambalam in Ernakulam district.
notes: Visible in Kerala's IT and football scene and speaks often (Khaleej Times, Onmanorama). Wikipedia article is flagged as possibly autobiographical, so check the details. No press email found on the IBS site; use the IBS website/LinkedIn.

name: Craig Kelleher
current_role: Co-Founder, Co-CIO and Managing Partner, Millstreet Capital Management (Boston); director of Diebold Nixdorf
profile: Craig M. Kelleher, CFA, co-founded Millstreet Capital Management in 2010 with Brian Connolly. The Boston firm invests in the small-to-mid-cap high-yield and leveraged-loan markets, including distressed situations. Through accounts Millstreet advises he is a 10%+ holder and director of ATM maker Diebold Nixdorf, which came out of its 2023 restructuring. He previously worked at Regiment Capital and at Morgan Stanley in leveraged finance.
interesting_fact: He sits on the boards of Canvas Energy and Trailblazer Energy Resources, and earlier co-founded Prelude Asset Management, a spinoff of Partners HealthCare that was sold to Congress Asset Management in 2010.
deep_cut_fact: Millstreet is named after the small town in County Cork, Ireland, where his father grew up. The logo's 'M' stands for Clara Mountain and the 'S' for the Blackwater River. He graduated Phi Beta Kappa from the University of Chicago (1999) and sits on its college advisory council.
notes: The DBD stake is held through Millstreet-advised accounts (sold down in 2025-26). Relevant to the energy theme through his oil and gas board seats. Best route is the Millstreet general inbox.

name: Mao Jun
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2021) with wealth from 'Viva' (pharmaceuticals), probably Viva Biotech (维亚生物, HKEX: 01873), but no source was found naming 毛隽. Viva Biotech's founder, chairman and CEO is Dr Mao Chen (毛晨/Cheney Mao), who founded it in 2008 as a structure-based drug discovery CRO.
notes: Identity unresolved. 毛隽 may be a Viva shareholder or a mistranscription of 毛晨 (Mao Chen). Check the HKEX substantial-shareholder disclosures before any outreach.

name: Luxtopholding Sarl Triton
current_role: Not a person: Triton LuxTopHolding SARL, a Luxembourg holding vehicle and Viasat (VSAT) shareholder whose ultimate general partner is Apax IX
profile: Triton LuxTopHolding SARL is a Luxembourg investment holding company (renamed June 2023) owned by Triton Lux EquityCo SARL and Connect Syndication L.P., with Apax IX as ultimate general partner. It has been selling down its Viasat stake: 3.75m shares at $9 in February 2025 left it with 4,795,334 shares (about 3.7%). It signed a stockholder agreement with Viasat in May 2025.
notes: Corporate/fund entity (Apax-affiliated), not an individual. No person to profile; drop it or redirect to the Apax partners behind the fund.
